segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
All the years that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years.
In the time of Seth, when his sons remembered the blessed life that was in Paradise,
they went up to Mount Hermon,
and lived in pure and holy conduct,
remaining far from marriage.
And on this account they were called 'Watchers' and 'Sons of God'.
Now that Seth, at the age of two hundred and five years, begot Enosh.
And all the years that Seth lived were nine hundred and twelve.
After Seth, Enosh his son.
He hoped (or sought? {OCR?}) to call upon the name of the Lord;
that is to say, even though he was drawn into marriage,
he did not neglect pleasing God,
more so than those who chose the virgin life and went up to the mountains,
and did not abide by their covenant.
Now that Enosh, at the age of one hundred and ninety years, begot Cainan.
All his life was nine hundred and five.
After {OCR?} his son.
At the age of one hundred and seventy, he begot Mahalaleel.
And all the years {OCR?} of his life were eight hundred and ten.
After Cainan, Mahalaleel his son.
At the age of one hundred and sixty-five years, he begot Jared.
And all the years of his life were eight hundred and ninety-five years.
After Mahalaleel, Jared {OCR?} his son.
At the age of one hundred and sixty-two years, he begot Enoch.
And all the years of his life were nine hundred and sixty-two years.
And in the fortieth year of Jared, that is, in the year one thousand of the world, the sons of God came down from Mount Hermon, about two hundred souls,
because they lost hope of returning to Paradise.
And when they lusted after sexual intercourse with women,
their brothers, the sons of Seth and Enosh, despised them,
and treated them as transgressors of the covenant, and did not agree to give them their daughters.
And on this account they went to the sons of Cain,
and took wives,
and begot men of renown—that is to say, famous in slaughter and plunder.
They also set up for themselves as first king a certain man whose name was Samyazos.
And when they began to stir up strife against their brothers, the sons of Seth,
they compelled them to also set up a king for themselves.
And they set up for themselves as first king a certain man whose name was Aloros;
and the second, Alparos;
and the third, Almilon;
and the fourth, Ammenon;
and the fifth, Megalaros;
and the sixth, Daonos the shepherd;
[footnote] {OCR?} ... and they kept their covenant.
